fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Front Entry Area; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Open Lawn Area
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Detached Structure Complexity
fr.recommendations:
• Trim vegetation along the driveway and front entry area to maintain clear sightlines for approaching responders.
• Cut back dense shrubs or overhanging branches that narrow the driveway or block the path to the front entry.
• Keep rear access points unlocked and clear of parked vehicles, equipment, or stored materials.
• Mark the rear access route with reflective markers so responders can locate it quickly at night or in low visibility.
• Post the address number at the driveway entrance in large, reflective characters visible from the street.
• Keep a second address marker on the main residence visible from the driveway approach.
• Clear a walking path between the main residence and the detached structure wide enough for two people to pass with equipment.
• Remove vegetation or stored items that block direct movement between the main residence and the detached structure.
• Keep both structures labeled or numbered if the detached structure has its own access door, so responders can quickly distinguish between them.
• Maintain the parking area clear of long-term stored vehicles that would reduce the space available for emergency vehicle staging.
• Thin dense plantings in the landscaped area adjacent to access routes so responders can move between the front and rear of the property without pushing through vegetation.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Green Space; Scattered Shrubs; Multiple Access Routes
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees in the scattered tree areas closest to structures to increase open space between the trees and buildings.
• Separate any tree clusters near structures by removing individual trees to break up the grouping.
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees near structures to reduce the chance of fire climbing from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Keep shrubs spread apart and away from the base of structures where scattered shrubs are present.
• Remove any dead or dry material from shrubs located near buildings or along access routes.
• Keep all access routes clear of low-hanging branches and overgrown vegetation along their edges.
• Maintain open green space areas by preventing shrub or tree encroachment into those open areas over time.
• Keep multiple access routes passable by trimming back any vegetation that narrows the travel lanes.
